exposure: disproportion of weight for gestational age
outcome: need for resuscitation of neonates in the delivery room
cohort: The study included 151 moderate and late preterm neonates born from May 2016 to May 2017 at a university hospital in southern Brazil.
finding: Obstetric factors (risk pregnancy, delivery complications, cesarean section, premature amniorrhexis) and neonatal factors (disproportion of weight for gestational age, lower gestational age, fetal malformation) were associated with the need for resuscitation in moderate and late preterm neonates.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was identified as an obstetric factor significantly associated with the need for resuscitation (p=0.005).
cross-section timing: Data was collected from medical records of births occurring from May 2016 to May 2017.
gest_age: Moderate and late preterm (not specified in weeks)
